gate1_cross_terrain_matrix.run: a100/eval_matrix.py, 37 cells, difficulty 0.5, 128 envs, 1200 steps -- go2_spec_flat/rough/stairs (HF, RohanRamesh/go2-specialists) + PAS oracle/estimator (HF, RohanRamesh/go2-pas-saro)
gate1_cross_terrain_matrix.verdict: GATE 1 PASSES on the informative columns: rough specialist wins rough (2.4x runner-up), stairs specialist wins stairs (1.4x, single-seed, provisional). flat is a 3-way tie at floor (0 falls). gaps/mixed catastrophic for every specialist (no gaps specialist exists). Both PAS modes excluded as degenerate (8-11% of commanded speed everywhere, bug #14) -- not competitive evidence either way. Read via falls/100m, not fall_pct (bug #15: fall_pct pools per episode, silently over-weights fast-cycling subpopulations -- caught via a mixed-terrain anomaly that took two rejected hypotheses (allocation rounding, commanded lateral drift) before landing on the real cause). Height-scan ablation: inconclusive as a gate-2 test (needs the generalist, job 11918, doesn't exist yet), but the stairs specialist shows a real positive scan-dependence on its home terrain (+30% falls/100m without the scan, while moving faster -- not just being more cautious). gaps ablation cells are artifacts (policy nearly stops moving, so 'falls less' is bug #1 again).
gate1_cross_terrain_matrix.caveats: Regenerate any pas_oracle number before trusting it against a cached file older than 2026-09-12 21:00 IST -- eval_matrix.py's resumable skip-if-exists logic silently reused pre-bug-#12-fix cells from an earlier same-day run once already.

switch_follow_2x2.run: unitree_rl_mjlab/scripts/switch_follow.py on course multi L1, follow task; go2_spec_flat/rough/stairs model_9999; calibration seeds 400/401 (512 trials/arm), confirmation seeds 500-502 (768 trials/arm); robustness: --obs-noise, --terminations saro, --level L2; scan-classifier arm
switch_follow_2x2.verdict: Switching beats the best fixed specialist (+15.0 pts as pre-registered, +4.2 with observation noise on). Optimum switch lead 0-0.3 m; switching >=0.8 m early is 7-17 pts worse and no better than never switching; 0.3 m late is 16-30 pts worse. Blending: no effect. Scan classifier matches ground-truth labels (within +-5 pts, both noise conditions). Anticipation hypothesis NOT supported. Generalist arm missing (no checkpoint).
switch_follow_2x2.caveats: Twin env has observation noise and pushes off unless --obs-noise (findings.md #22). Under orientation-only falls nothing separates at L1. Specialists are weak (curriculum collapse at iteration 5000).

go2_generalist.run: switch_follow.py, course multi L1, follow task, fixed:generalist vs hard:0.3:label vs fixed:stairs; seeds 500-502 and replication 503-505, 256 trials each, observation noise off and on (1536 trials/arm/condition)
go2_generalist.verdict: Noise off: generalist 90.5% vs switching 89.3% (-1.2 pts, CI -3.4..+0.9) -- no difference. Noise on: generalist 82.5% vs switching 90.9% (+8.4, CI +6.0..+10.8). Two runs agree. Walking, not bracing (lost 0%, tracking error 0.170 vs 0.169, same traverse time). Pinned terrain d=0.5 (eval_matrix, 128 envs): 0.00 / 4.70 / 8.33 falls per 100 m on flat / rough / stairs, i.e. close to the best specialist per column. Iteration-4800 checkpoint is WORSE than 9999 on the course (73.2% vs 90.6% noise off; 75.3% vs 83.7% noise on), so no undamaged generalist exists. Height-scan ablation: falls/100m 0.00/4.70/8.33 -> 65.4/188.4/67.0 on flat/rough/stairs.

go2_spec_stairs_it4800.run: switch_follow.py with --extra-policy stairs=<model_4800>; L1 seeds 500-502 (noise off and on), L2 seeds 600-601 (noise off); fixed arms + hard leads -0.3/0/0.3/0.8/1.5
go2_spec_stairs_it4800.verdict: Stairs-alone crosses the mixed course 97.7% at L1 (94.9% noise on), 82.8% at L2, vs 76.6 / 83.2 / 33.4 for model_9999. Switching adds nothing at L1 (-1.0, CI -2.8..+0.7), +3.7 at L2 (CI -0.7..+8.1). Early switching free (1.5 vs 0.3 m: +0.7, +0.8, +1.0, all CIs include 0); lip failures gone. Late switching worse than ever at L2 (boundary 39.8%, 0.3 m late 21.3% vs 86.5% at 0.3 m ahead).
go2_spec_stairs_it4800.caveats: Follow task on the multi course, not the single-obstacle goal-controller courses of Phase 1 (findings.md #23 explains why the follow task is the one used). One earlier checkpoint of one run, not a retrain.

go2_spec_stairs_v2.run: scripts/switch_follow_stairs_ckpt.sh TAG=stairsv2: L1 seeds 500-502 (noise off and on), L2 seeds 600-601; fixed arms + hard leads -0.3/0/0.3/0.8/1.5
go2_spec_stairs_v2.verdict: Best policy in the project. Alone: 99.7% L1, 99.9% L1 noise on, 95.5% L2 (model_4800: 97.7/94.9/82.8; as trained: 76.6/83.2/33.4). Switching adds nothing (+0.3, 0.0, +0.8, CIs include 0); early switching free (-0.1, 0.0, +1.4); 0.3 m late costs 17-29 pts at L1, 66 at L2. REAL RISERS (2026-10-05, 5-step flight, noise on, crossing rate up/down): 9 cm 84/100, 12 cm 0/69, 15 cm 0/8, 17 cm 0/1; stalls going up. Randomised layouts: 92.7% alone; 9.2% without its scan. Scan faults: 200 ms delay -0.5, 60% stale -2.0, +-6 cm bias -19.1.

go2_generalist_v2.run: switch_follow_generalist.sh EXPERIMENT=go2_generalist_v2, stairs slot = stairs v2; L1 seeds 500-505 noise off and on; L2 seeds 600-601
go2_generalist_v2.verdict: Alone: 64.9% L1 (72.7% noise on), 15.8% L2 -- WORSE than the first generalist (90.5/82.5 at L1; 10.9 at L2). Stairs v2 alone 99.9/99.8/95.3; switching 99.9/99.8/96.7. Walking, not bracing (lost 0%); fails on the down-stairs. Holding the command range is not a general fix.

randomised_layouts.run: scripts/switch_follow_random_layouts.sh 900 919: 20 random layouts (4 L1, 16 L2), noise on, 128 trials each; bank A stairs=v2, bank B stairs=as trained
randomised_layouts.verdict: Mean over layouts: stairs v2 alone 92.7%, switch 0.3 92.1%, switch 1.5 93.9%, 0.3 m late 27.8%, stairs v2 without scan 9.2%, generalist v1 14.6%, v2 37.5%; as-trained stairs alone 35.2%, switch 0.3 35.4%, switch 1.5 36.3%. Stairs v2 ahead of each generalist and the as-trained specialist in 20/20 layouts. Switching adds nothing with either bank. The fixed-course +15 pt switching advantage and early-switch penalty do NOT hold across layouts.

go2_spec_stairs_v3.run: switch_follow.py single flights, 128 trials each, noise on: stairs_up 0.09 and 0.15 m, stairs_down 0.15 m, next to stairs v2 in the same runs
go2_spec_stairs_v3.verdict: FAILED RUN, do not use. Crosses 0/128 in all three cells with 0 falls and 100% lost: it does not move, even on the flat approach. Confirms the cluster's reading (12% of commanded speed). Stairs v2 in the same runs: 80.5% up at 9 cm.

go2_spec_stairs_v4_kn_it400.run: switch_follow.py single flights, 128 trials, noise on: stairs up/down at 0.09 and 0.12 m; go2_spec_stairs_v4a_kn and _v4b_kn model_400 next to stairs v2
go2_spec_stairs_v4_kn_it400.verdict: Both cross 0% in all four cells with 0 falls and 100% lost, tracking error 0.92 m/s: they cannot keep up with the leader on the flat approach. Stairs v2 same runs: 9 cm 83% up / 98% down; 12 cm 0% / 66%.

notes: Existing eval numbers in findings.md were produced by SLURM eval jobs run ON THE CLUSTER, not this laptop pipeline -- this pipeline is new as of 2026-09-11 and adds the ability to spot-check checkpoints locally (specialists especially, since those never touch HF) without spending cluster queue time. laptop_pull_and_eval.sh defaults to --num-envs 256, empirically confirmed on this machine's 8GB RTX 5060 Laptop GPU on 2026-09-11 (ran Unitree-Go2-PAS-Oracle task, stage2/model_79998.pt, estimator-only mode, 200 steps, no OOM, GPU memory fully released after). Not yet pushed higher -- the cluster's own eval default is 1024 envs, so there may be headroom, but that hasn't been tested here. If a checkpoint's eval genuinely doesn't fit at a reasonable env count, say so explicitly rather than silently shrinking further and treating it as equivalent.
